components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The main action on onboarding and other focused flows.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { width: 100%; max-width: 350px; height: 45px; border: 0; border-radius: 8px; background: var(--kd-primary); color: var(--kd-white); padding: 0 20px; font: 700 16px/1.2 Satoshi, sans-serif; cursor: pointer; transition: opacity 160ms ease, transform 160ms ease; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { opacity: .92; } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: scale(.985); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--kd-primary); outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: A reversed action on a coffee-brown branded surface.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { width: 100%; max-width: 350px; height: 45px; border: 0; border-radius: 8px; background: var(--kd-white); color: var(--kd-primary); padding: 0 20px; font: 700 16px/1.2 Satoshi, sans-serif; cursor: pointer; transition: opacity 160ms ease, transform 160ms ease; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { opacity: .94; } .ds-btn-secondary:active { transform: scale(.985); } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--kd-white); outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Search Field
components.description: A white search field used over the dark home hero.
components.css: .ds-search { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 11px; height: 50px; padding: 0 16px; border-radius: 8px; background: var(--kd-white); color: var(--kd-ink-50); } .ds-search input { width: 100%; border: 0; outline: 0; background: transparent; color: var(--kd-ink); font: 400 12px/1.35 Satoshi, sans-serif; } .ds-search input::placeholder { color: var(--kd-ink-50); } .ds-search:focus-within { box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px var(--kd-white), 0 0 0 4px var(--kd-primary); }

components.name: Cafe Card
components.description: A compact result card pairing a cafe image with work-readiness metadata.
components.html:

components.css: .ds-cafe-card { display: flex; min-height: 100px; overflow: hidden; border-radius: 8px; background: var(--kd-white); box-shadow: 0 0 8px var(--kd-shadow); } .ds-cafe-photo { width: 90px; height: 100px; flex: 0 0 90px; background: var(--kd-placeholder); } .ds-cafe-body { min-width: 0; padding: 11px 13px 10px 15px; color: var(--kd-ink); font: 400 12px/1.35 Satoshi, sans-serif; } .ds-cafe-status { color: var(--kd-success); font: 700 10px/1.2 Satoshi, sans-serif; } .ds-cafe-body h3 { margin: 3px 0 0; color: var(--kd-primary); font: 700 16px/1.375 Satoshi, sans-serif; } .ds-cafe-body p { margin: 0; white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; } .ds-cafe-body small { display: block; margin-top: 8px; }

components.name: Filter Chip
components.description: A compact horizontally scrolling filter with an unmistakable active state.
components.css: .ds-chip-active { width: 97px; height: 27px; padding: 0; border: 0; border-radius: 4px; background: var(--kd-primary); color: var(--kd-white); font: 700 12px/1.2 Satoshi, sans-serif; white-space: nowrap; cursor: pointer; } .ds-chip-active:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--kd-primary); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Bottom Navigation
components.css: .ds-tabbar { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(4, 1fr); align-items: center; height: 100px; padding: 0 12px; background: var(--kd-white-80); backdrop-filter: blur(4px); } .ds-tabbar-item { display: grid; place-items: center; height: 48px; border: 0; background: transparent; color: var(--kd-primary-25); font-size: 24px; cursor: pointer; } .ds-tabbar-item-active { color: var(--kd-white); } .ds-tabbar-item-active::before { content: ''; position: absolute; width: 30px; height: 30px; border-radius: 5px; background: var(--kd-primary); z-index: -1; } .ds-tabbar-item:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--kd-primary); outline-offset: 3px; border-radius: 8px; } .ds-sr-only { position: absolute; width: 1px; height: 1px; overflow: hidden; clip: rect(0, 0, 0, 0); }

narrative.overview:
KapeDoko’s current visual system feels like a dependable neighborhood counter: warm, familiar, and immediately useful. A dark coffee-brown anchor gives the interface a recognizable home, while white content surfaces keep practical cafe information easy to scan. The system is compact and phone-first, with a little editorial warmth in featured cafe imagery and the logo-led onboarding.

Controls are quietly tactile rather than decorative. Small rounded corners, short labels, focused status colors, and restrained card shadows help people make a decision while they are already out in the city. The product’s visual language supports the work-readiness mission: amenities, open status, and location remain more actionable than atmosphere.
keyCharacteristics: Coffee-brown brand anchor with warm cream support
Compact mobile density with generous touch targets
Rounded 4–8px surfaces and pill-shaped progress indicators
Tonal depth through white surfaces and subtle ambient shadows
Logo and amenity iconography used as recognizable product cues

rules.name: The Coffee-Brown Anchor Rule
rules.body: Coffee-brown anchors primary actions and major branded surfaces; status colors communicate state rather than replacing the brand color.

rules.name: The Quiet Depth Rule
rules.body: Use tonal contrast and small ambient shadows to separate surfaces; avoid heavy floating panels.

dos: Do use coffee-brown as the visual anchor for branded surfaces, active states, and primary actions.
Do keep cafe metadata short, legible, and easy to scan on a phone.
Do preserve the existing KapeDoko logo, wordmark, watermark, and onboarding graphic assets.
Do expose WiFi, power outlet, hours, and location information as text or accessible names alongside icons.
Do respect safe-area insets and reduced-motion preferences across web and native shells.
donts: Don't make atmosphere, stock photography, or placeholder cafe data more prominent than work-readiness facts.
Don't replace the coffee-brown anchor with a new brand color without an explicit identity decision.
Don't use icons alone to communicate amenities or status.
Don't introduce heavy borders, dramatic shadows, or dense desktop-only layouts that break the compact mobile rhythm.
Don't treat sample cafe names, ratings, or Unsplash photography as evidence of real coverage.
